posts.title: Sonita’s Norwegian Rice Pudding with an Indian Twist
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Sonita’s Norwegian Rice Pudding with an Indian Twist | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A baked brown-rice pudding with cinnamon, cardamom, raisins, milk, and cream, adapted with a nutty short-grain rice base.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.238
posts.body_markdown:
Sonita’s Norwegian Rice Pudding with an Indian Twist bakes cooked short-grain brown rice with milk, cream, raisins, cinnamon, cardamom, and brown sugar.

The brown rice gives the pudding a nuttier base than a conventional white-rice version. Everything is assembled directly in a buttered baking dish, so the preparation is unusually simple.

The pudding needs 30–40 minutes in a moderate oven. During that time the milk and cream reduce around the rice while the whole spices perfume the mixture.

## Ingredients
- Butter, for greasing the baking dish
- 2 1/2 cups short-grain brown rice, cooked
- 1/2–3/4 cup brown sugar
- 2–3 cinnamon sticks, about 2 inches (5 cm) long
- 1 cup heavy cream
- 4–5 cardamom pods, slit at the end
- 1/2 cup raisins
- 2 1/2 cups whole milk

## Method
Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Butter an ovenproof baking dish and spread the cooked rice across the bottom. Add the brown sugar, cinnamon, cream, cardamom, raisins, and milk and stir to combine. Bake for 30–40 minutes. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Traditional Indian Rice Pudding with Nuts
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Traditional Indian Rice Pudding with Nuts | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A quick stovetop rice pudding with milk, nutmeg, cinnamon, raisins, pistachios, almonds, and an optional saffron variation.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.239
posts.body_markdown:
Traditional Indian Rice Pudding with Nuts turns cooked, mashed rice into a quick stovetop pudding with milk, warm spices, sweetener, raisins, and chopped nuts.

Because the rice is already cooked, the pudding comes together in one pot in about 20 minutes. Nutmeg and cinnamon season the milk while raisins add sweetness and texture.

Pistachios and almonds are kept out of the simmering mixture and added at the end. The source also offers a saffron variation that is soaked in milk before joining the pot.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup rice, cooked and mashed
- 4 cups whole milk
- 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg
- 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon, or one 2-inch piece cinnamon bark or stick
- 4 tablespoons sweetener
- 3 tablespoons raisins
- 1 teaspoon pistachios, coarsely chopped, for garnish
- 1 teaspoon almonds, coarsely chopped, for garnish
- Optional variation: 1/4 teaspoon broken saffron strands plus 2 tablespoons milk

## Method
Combine the rice, milk, nutmeg, cinnamon, sweetener, and raisins in a large pot over high heat and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Garnish with the pistachios and almonds and serve. For the saffron variation, soak the saffron in 2 tablespoons milk for 10 minutes and add it with the other ingredients. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Rasgouli Homemade Cheese Patties in Sweet Syrup
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Rasgouli Homemade Cheese Patties in Sweet Syrup | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Fresh homemade cheese patties are kneaded with semolina, simmered in rose-scented maple syrup, then chilled so the syrup can soak in.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.240
posts.body_markdown:
Rasgouli Homemade Cheese Patties in Sweet Syrup begins by making fresh cheese from milk, yogurt, and lemon juice, then kneading it with semolina until smooth.

The cheese is shaped into small balls and simmered gently in a maple-syrup mixture scented with rose water. Keeping the balls covered with syrup as they cook helps them absorb sweetness evenly.

After simmering, the rasgouli is chilled for at least 30 minutes and can rest overnight for a deeper syrup flavor. The source also gives a traditional white-sugar syrup alternative.

## Ingredients
- 6 1/2 cups whole milk
- 1 cup plain yogurt
- 3 tablespoons lemon juice
- 1 1/2 tablespoons semolina flour
- 1 1/2 cups maple syrup
- 1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar
- 1 1/2 cups water
- 1/2 teaspoon rose water
- Traditional syrup option: 3 cups white sugar in place of maple syrup, with an additional 1 1/2 cups water

## Method
Bring the milk to a boil in a large pot, remove it from the heat, and stir in the yogurt and lemon juice until curds separate. Strain through cheesecloth, cool for about 10 minutes, then squeeze out the whey. Knead the cheese for 2–3 minutes, then add the semolina gradually, about 1/2 teaspoon at a time, and knead for another 8–10 minutes until firm and smooth. For the syrup, boil the maple syrup, cream of tartar, and 1 1/2 cups water for about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, add the rose water, reserve 1 cup of syrup, and keep the remaining syrup on the lowest heat. Shape tablespoon portions of cheese into small balls and add them to the hot syrup. Simmer for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding reserved syrup as needed so the balls remain covered. Remove from the heat and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or overnight. Serve warm or cool with syrup. Makes 6 servings.

posts.title: Light Carrot Halva
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A lighter carrot halva in which grated carrots cook slowly with whole spices, saffron, milk, cream, and a final nut garnish.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.241
posts.body_markdown:
Light Carrot Halva slowly cooks a large quantity of grated carrots with whole spices, then finishes them with milk, cream, saffron, and sweetener.

Cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon are warmed briefly in oil and ghee before the carrots go in. The carrots then cook for 25–30 minutes, building sweetness without scorching.

Milk, cream, and saffron are added only after the carrots have softened. The mixture is cooked until the liquid is absorbed, then sweetened and reduced until it pulls cleanly from the pan.

## Ingredients
- 1/4 teaspoon saffron strands, broken
- 2 tablespoons whole milk, for soaking the saffron
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1 tablespoon ghee or butter
- 3 cloves
- 4 cardamom pods, slit at the end
- 2–3 pieces cinnamon bark, about 2 inches (5 cm) long
- 6–8 cups grated carrots, about 2 1/2 lb (1 kg)
- 1 cup whole milk
- 1/2 cup cream
- 1/2 cup sweetener
- 10 almonds or pistachios, or a combination, coarsely ground, for garnish
- Optional variation: 1/4 cup raisins or currants

## Method
Soak the saffron in 2 tablespoons milk. Heat the oil and ghee in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the cloves, cardamom, and cinnamon and stir for 1 minute. Add the carrots and cook for 25–30 minutes, stirring frequently and adding a little more ghee or oil if needed to prevent scorching. Add the milk, cream, and saffron milk and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is absorbed. Add the sweetener, reduce the heat to low, and continue cooking until the mixture no longer clings to the side of the pot. Transfer to a flat serving plate and garnish with the nuts. If using raisins or currants, add them with the sweetener. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Sweet Shikand
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A chilled shikand of light sour cream, cardamom, saffron, and almonds that rests for three hours before serving.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.242
posts.body_markdown:
Sweet Shikand is a chilled sour-cream dessert flavored with sugar, cardamom, saffron, and ground almonds, then finished with mint and more almonds.

There is no cooking in the base recipe. Its key step is time: the mixed dessert rests in the refrigerator for at least three hours so the saffron can color and flavor the cream.

A final stir before serving redistributes the saffron and almonds. The mint garnish keeps the finish fresh against the rich, sweet dairy base.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups light sour cream
- 4 tablespoons sugar
- 1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom
- 1/4 teaspoon saffron strands, broken
- 2 tablespoons almonds, coarsely ground
- 1 teaspoon almonds, coarsely ground, for garnish
- 3 fresh mint leaves, for garnish

## Method
Combine the sour cream, sugar, cardamom, saffron, and 2 tablespoons ground almonds in a bowl and mix well. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours. Stir again before serving, then garnish with the remaining almonds and mint leaves. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Michele’s Shikand
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A ricotta-and-cream variation on shikand with three source options: banana-raisin, coconut-fennel, or pear with peppercorn and cinnamon.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.243
posts.body_markdown:
Michele’s Shikand changes the Sweet Shikand base by replacing the sour cream with ricotta and whipping cream and increasing the ground almonds.

This dessert is intentionally flexible. The source offers three directions: banana or raisin with ginger and cinnamon, coconut or fennel, or pear cooked into a peppercorn-and-cinnamon compote.

Each variation is folded into the shikand before chilling, so the dessert keeps the same cold, set character while taking on a different fruit or spice profile.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup ricotta cheese
- 1 cup whipping cream
- 4 tablespoons sugar
- 1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom
- 1/4 teaspoon saffron strands, broken
- 3 tablespoons almonds, coarsely ground, plus 1 teaspoon for garnish
- 3 fresh mint leaves, for garnish
- Variation 1: 1/2 teaspoon ghee, 1/4 teaspoon minced ginger, one 2-inch (5-cm) cinnamon bark piece, 1 cup sliced bananas and/or 1/4 cup raisins
- Variation 2: 2 tablespoons grated coconut and/or 1/2 teaspoon fennel seeds
- Variation 3: 1/2 teaspoon ghee, 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground red peppercorns, 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon, 1 cup chopped pear, and up to 2 tablespoons water if needed

## Method
Mix the ricotta, whipping cream, sugar, cardamom, saffron, and 3 tablespoons ground almonds, then use one of the source variations before refrigerating. For the banana-raisin version, heat the ghee over medium-high, sauté the ginger and cinnamon bark for 30 seconds to 1 minute, add the banana and/or raisins, and fold into the shikand; remove the cinnamon before serving. For the coconut-fennel version, simply stir those ingredients into the mixture. For the pear version, heat the ghee, add the peppercorns and cinnamon, then cook the pear until soft and compote-like, adding up to 2 tablespoons water if needed; cool slightly and fold in. Refrigerate before serving and garnish with almonds and mint.

posts.title: Saffron, Cranberry & Almond Vermicelli
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Roasted vermicelli is browned with whole spices, then baked with saffron, cranberries, milk, and agave before an almond finish.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.244
posts.body_markdown:
Saffron, Cranberry & Almond Vermicelli browns roasted vermicelli with cardamom and cinnamon before finishing it with milk, agave, cranberries, saffron, and almonds.

The dish starts on the stovetop, where the vermicelli is sautéed until evenly browned. Water, milk, sweetener, fruit, and saffron are then brought briefly to a boil.

The final cooking happens in the oven: first covered so the vermicelli absorbs the liquid, then uncovered so the remaining moisture evaporates.

## Ingredients
- 1/4 teaspoon saffron strands, crushed
- 1/2 cup water, for soaking the saffron
- 2 tablespoons good oil
- 6 cardamom pods, slit at the end
- 2 cinnamon sticks
- 2 cups roasted vermicelli, broken into pieces
- 1 cup water
- 1/2 cup skim milk
- 1/3 cup agave nectar or other sweetener
- 1 1/2 tablespoons dried cranberries
- 1 1/2 tablespoons almonds, coarsely ground, for garnish

## Method
Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Combine the saffron with 1/2 cup water and set aside. Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat, add the cardamom and cinnamon, and sauté for 30 seconds. Add the vermicelli and sauté until evenly browned. Add 1 cup water, the milk, agave, cranberries, and saffron water, increase the heat, and bring to a boil. Remove from the heat, transfer to a covered ovenproof dish, and bake for 10 minutes. Remove the lid and bake for another 10 minutes, until the liquid has evaporated. Remove the whole spices, garnish with almonds, and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Lapsi
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A cracked-wheat lapsi toasted in ghee, simmered with milk, coconut and spices, then baked and finished with almonds and pistachios.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.245
posts.body_markdown:
Lapsi is a grainy cracked-wheat dessert enriched with ghee, milk, coconut, cardamom, raisins, and optional saffron, then finished with nuts.

The cracked wheat is toasted in ghee with cinnamon before any liquid is added. This early cooking step gives the grain a deeper flavor before it softens in milk and water.

After simmering until the liquid is absorbed, the mixture is transferred to the oven for a final covered bake. Almonds and pistachios are added only at serving.

## Ingredients
- 2 tablespoons ghee or good oil
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 1 cup cracked wheat
- 1 cup whole milk
- 2 cups water
- 1/4 teaspoon saffron strands, broken, optional
- 2 tablespoons shredded coconut
- 3 cardamom pods, slit at the end
- 1/2–3/4 cup sweetener
- 2 tablespoons raisins
- 1 teaspoon almonds, coarsely ground, for garnish
- 1 teaspoon pistachios, coarsely ground, for garnish

## Method
Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Melt the ghee in a pot over medium heat, add the cinnamon, and cook for 30 seconds. Add the cracked wheat and cook for about 6 minutes, stirring constantly. Add the milk, water, optional saffron, coconut, and cardamom and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the sweetener and raisins and simmer for about 15 minutes, stirring, until the liquid is absorbed. Transfer to a covered ovenproof dish and bake for 20 minutes. Garnish with almonds and pistachios. Remove the whole spices before serving if preferred. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Kara
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A warm whole-wheat kara in which browned flour and ghee are whisked with hot sugar syrup and milk, with optional spice and nut variations.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.246
posts.body_markdown:
Kara, also called Shiro in the source, is a warm whole-wheat dessert made by browning flour in ghee, then whisking in sweetened water and hot milk.

Three pots move in parallel: one for the sugar syrup, one for the flour and ghee, and one for the milk. Bringing the components together while hot keeps the mixture smooth.

The base version is deliberately plain, but the source provides optional saffron, nutmeg, cardamom, nuts, pistachios, and poppy seeds for a more aromatic finish.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup water
- 1/2 cup brown sugar
- 1/4 cup ghee or butter
- 1 cup whole wheat flour
- 1 cup whole milk
- Variation 1: 3/4 cup gur in place of brown sugar
- Variation 2: 1/4 teaspoon broken saffron strands, 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
- Variation 3: 1 tablespoon slivered almonds, 1 tablespoon crushed pistachios, and 1 teaspoon white poppy seeds, for garnish

## Method
Bring the water and brown sugar to a boil in one pot, then reduce the heat to medium. In a second pot over medium heat, melt the ghee, add the flour, and stir constantly until golden brown. In a third pot, heat the milk until it just begins to boil, then remove it from the heat. Whisk the hot sugar-water mixture into the browned flour and ghee until smooth and thick. Add the hot milk, reduce the heat to low, and cook for about 20 minutes, stirring often. Use any of the source variations if desired. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: China Grass Pudding with Nuts
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: China Grass Pudding with Nuts | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: An agar-set milk and cream pudding flavored with vanilla or rose water, chilled until firm, and finished with almonds and pistachios.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.247
posts.body_markdown:
China Grass Pudding with Nuts uses agar agar to set a milk-and-cream pudding flavored with vanilla or rose water and finished with almonds and pistachios.

The agar agar is fully dissolved in boiling water before the sweetener, milk, and cream are added. That sequence gives the setting agent time to disperse evenly.

The pudding is cooled before the nut garnish is added, then refrigerated for about four hours until firm. The source also offers a saffron variation soaked in milk first.

## Ingredients
- 2 1/2 tablespoons agar agar flakes
- 1 cup water
- 1 cup sweetener
- 4 cups whole milk
- 1 cup whipping cream
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, or a few drops rose water
- 1 tablespoon almonds, slivered
- 1 tablespoon pistachios, coarsely ground, for garnish
- Optional variation: 1/4 teaspoon broken saffron strands

## Method
Bring the agar agar and water to a boil in a large pot over high heat and boil for 2 minutes, stirring until dissolved. Add the sweetener and stir to dissolve. Add the milk and whipping cream and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from the heat, stir in the vanilla or rose water, and let the mixture cool slightly. Pour into a serving bowl. When completely cool, garnish with the nuts and refrigerate for about 4 hours, until firm. For the saffron variation, soak the saffron in the milk for 10 minutes before adding it to the pot. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Fruity “Jello”
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Fresh fruit is set in a light apple-juice and agar mixture for a simple chilled dessert that firms in under an hour.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.248
posts.body_markdown:
Fruity “Jello” is a simple fruit dessert set with agar agar rather than gelatin. Fresh fruit sits in a light mixture of water and apple juice.

The agar agar is boiled in water for 2–3 minutes until dissolved, then the apple juice is stirred in off the heat. This keeps the method short and direct.

The liquid is poured over the prepared fruit and chilled for 45–60 minutes. Once set, the dessert can be served directly from the bowl.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups fruit of your choice, sliced or chopped
- 1 cup water
- 1 tablespoon agar agar flakes
- 1 1/2 cups apple juice

## Method
Place the prepared fruit in a serving bowl. Combine the water and agar agar in a medium pot over high heat and boil for 2–3 minutes, stirring until the agar dissolves. Remove from the heat, stir in the apple juice, and pour the mixture over the fruit. Refrigerate for 45–60 minutes, or until set. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: The Long-Awaited Chai Crème Brûlée
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: The Long-Awaited Chai Crème Brûlée | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A chai-spiced crème brûlée infused with tea, fennel, clove, cardamom, cinnamon, and ginger, then baked in a water bath and caramelized.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.249
posts.body_markdown:
The Long-Awaited Chai Crème Brûlée infuses whipping cream with fennel, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, Earl Grey, and black tea before making the custard.

The spiced cream is heated only until it begins to foam, then covered and steeped for 10 minutes. After straining, it is reheated and used gradually to temper the egg yolks and sugar.

The custards bake in a water bath for one hour, then chill until set. A final layer of sugar is melted into a hard crust with a hot spoon or small blowtorch.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup fennel seeds
- 1 tablespoon cloves
- 1 1/2 tablespoons cardamom seeds
- 2 cinnamon sticks
- 1 large slice fresh ginger
- 4 cups whipping cream
- 2–3 Earl Grey tea bags, regular or decaf
- 2 tablespoons black tea leaves, or 2–3 black tea bags, regular or decaf
- 12 egg yolks
- 1 cup sugar
- 1/2 cup sugar, for the brûléed topping

## Method
Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Combine the fennel, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, and ginger. Heat the spice mixture with the cream, Earl Grey, and black tea over medium-high heat until it just begins to foam and bubble, then remove from the heat, cover, and steep for 10 minutes. Strain into a clean pot, return to the heat, and bring to a boil uncovered, then remove from the heat. Mix the egg yolks with 1 cup sugar. Temper the yolks by adding the hot cream 1 tablespoon at a time while stirring constantly. Strain the custard and divide among 12 ramekins. Set the ramekins in a deep baking dish with about 1/2 inch (1 1/4 cm) of water and bake for 1 hour. Cool and refrigerate until set. Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup sugar over the custards and melt it into a hard crust with a heated spoon or small blowtorch. Makes 12 servings.

posts.title: Caroline’s White Chocolate Cardamom Mousse
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Caroline’s White Chocolate Cardamom Mousse | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A chilled white-chocolate mousse made with cardamom-infused coconut milk, gelatin, vanilla, and stiffly beaten egg whites.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.250
posts.body_markdown:
Caroline’s White Chocolate Cardamom Mousse infuses coconut milk with crushed cardamom, then combines it with melted white chocolate, gelatin, vanilla, and whipped egg whites.

The cardamom is boiled briefly with the coconut milk and removed before the gelatin and chocolate are incorporated. Melting the chocolate separately helps keep the mixture smooth.

The mousse chills in two stages: 30 minutes before the egg whites are folded in, then another 90 minutes so the finished mousse can set.

## Ingredients
- 6 cardamom pods, crushed
- 1 3/4 cups coconut milk
- 7 oz (200 g) white chocolate, at room temperature and chopped
- 1 package gelatin, sized for 4 servings
- 1 tablespoon confectioner’s sugar, optional
- 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
- 2 egg whites

## Method
Bring the cardamom and coconut milk to a boil in a large pot over high heat. Remove from the heat and lift out the cardamom pods. Melt the white chocolate in a double boiler or over very low heat, stirring constantly. Return the coconut milk to the heat, sprinkle in the gelatin, and stir until completely dissolved. Sift in the optional confectioner’s sugar and stir to dissolve. Remove from the heat, add the vanilla and melted chocolate, and whisk vigorously until smooth. Pour into a bowl, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Beat the egg whites until stiff, fold them into the chilled chocolate mixture, and refrigerate for another 90 minutes. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Creamy Extra Dark Chocolate Fondue
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Creamy Extra Dark Chocolate Fondue | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A simple dark-chocolate fondue made by pouring boiling soy milk or cream over 70% chocolate and serving it with mixed fruit.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.251
posts.body_markdown:
Creamy Extra Dark Chocolate Fondue is built from just dark chocolate and hot soy milk or cream, with mixed fruit served alongside for dipping.

The chocolate is not cooked directly. Instead, boiling soy milk is poured over chopped 70% dark chocolate and stirred until the mixture becomes smooth and glossy.

The fruit provides the texture and contrast, so the source keeps the chocolate mixture simple. Orange, strawberries, banana, cherries, and pineapple are given as examples.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup 70% cocoa-mass dark chocolate, chopped or broken into pieces
- 1 cup soy milk or whipping cream
- 5–6 cups mixed fruit, such as orange segments, strawberries, sliced bananas, cherries, or sliced pineapple

## Method
Place the chopped chocolate in an ovenproof bowl. Bring the soy milk or whipping cream to a boil in a medium pot over high heat, then immediately remove it from the heat and pour it over the chocolate. Stir until smooth. Arrange the fruit on a platter and serve with forks or fondue sticks for dipping. Makes 6 servings.

posts.title: Caroline’s Carob Almond Cookies
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Carob almond cookies made with coconut oil, maple syrup, almond meal, flour, and carob chips, with crisp edges and softer centers.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.252
posts.body_markdown:
Caroline’s Carob Almond Cookies combine coconut oil and maple syrup with carob, almond meal, oat flour, salt, and carob chips or nuts.

The wet and dry mixtures are prepared separately, then combined into a dark dough. Tablespoon portions are flattened into circles before baking.

The cookies bake only until the edges turn crisp and remain softer in the center. Cooling them on the baking sheet helps them set before they are moved to a rack.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup coconut oil or butter, at room temperature
- 1/2 cup maple syrup, at room temperature
- 1/2 cup carob powder
- 1 cup almond meal
- 2/3 cup oat flour, kamut flour, or unbleached white flour
- Pinch of salt
- 1/3 cup carob chips or nuts of your choice

## Method
Preheat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Mix the coconut oil and maple syrup in one bowl. In another bowl, combine the carob powder, almond meal, flour, and salt, then stir in the carob chips or nuts. Add the oil mixture to the dry ingredients and stir until a dark dough forms. Place tablespoon-sized balls on a lightly greased baking sheet, press them into circles, and bake for about 12 minutes, until the edges are crisp. Cool on the baking sheet before transferring to a rack. The centers should remain a little soft. Makes 14–18 cookies.

posts.title: Caroline’s Vanilla Cardamom Shortbread Cookies
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Caroline’s Vanilla Cardamom Shortbread Cookies | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Vanilla-cardamom shortbread baked as a thick slab, topped with sliced almonds near the end, then cooled and cut into crisp squares.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.253
posts.body_markdown:
Caroline’s Vanilla Cardamom Shortbread Cookies pair a classic butter-and-sugar shortbread base with vanilla, ground cardamom, and sliced almonds.

The dough is intentionally stiff and crumbly. Rather than shaping individual cookies first, it is pressed into a thick rectangle and baked as one slab.

Almonds are added after the first 30 minutes and pressed into the surface before a final 10-minute bake. The slab is sliced only after a brief cooling period.

## Ingredients
- 1 cup butter
- 1/2 cup sugar, such as Sucanat, Rapadura, or gur
- 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
- 4 cups spelt flour or unbleached white flour
- 1 tablespoon ground cardamom
- 1/2 cup sliced almonds

## Method
Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Cream the butter and sugar in an electric mixer or food processor, then blend in the vanilla. In a separate bowl, mix the flour and cardamom. Fold the flour mixture into the creamed butter and sugar to form a stiff, crumbly dough. Press the dough into an even rectangle about 1 inch (2 1/2 cm) thick on a greased baking sheet and bake for 30 minutes. Sprinkle the almonds over the surface, press them into the dough, and bake for another 10 minutes, until the shortbread begins to turn golden. Cool on the baking sheet for 10 minutes, slice into squares, and let the cookies cool completely and become crisp before removing them. Makes 25–30 cookies.

posts.title: Blackberry-Apple Oat Bars
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Apple and blackberry bars with a shared oat-and-flour mixture used for both the baked base and the crumble topping.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.254
posts.body_markdown:
Blackberry-Apple Oat Bars use one oat-and-flour mixture for both the base and the crumble topping, with sliced apples and blackberries layered between them.

Half the mixture is pressed into the pan and baked first so the bottom develops structure before the fruit is added. The reserved half becomes the crumbly top layer.

The bars need to cool before cutting so the fruit filling and oat layers can set. The source makes a large tray yielding 12–15 bars.

## Ingredients
- 3/4 cup unbleached white flour
- 3/4 cup whole wheat flour
- 2 cups rolled oats
- 1 1/2 cups slivered almonds, or a mix of sunflower and pumpkin seeds
- 2 teaspoons baking powder
- 1 teaspoon cinnamon
- 1 cup ghee or unsalted butter, softened
- 1 cup Sucanat, raw cane sugar, or brown sugar
- 4 apples, cored and cut into slivers
- 3 cups blackberries

## Method
Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C). In a blender or food processor, combine the flours, oats, almonds or seeds, baking powder, cinnamon, ghee or butter, and sugar. Reserve half of the mixture. Press the remaining half into the bottom of a lightly oiled 10 x 15-inch (25 x 38-cm) baking sheet and bake for 10–12 minutes, until lightly browned. Arrange the apple slivers over the crust, add the blackberries, and scatter the reserved crumble mixture over the top. Bake for another 15–20 minutes. Cool before cutting into bars. Makes 12–15 bars.

posts.title: Creamy Banana-Berry Ice
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Frozen bananas, lime, berries, and coconut cream blend into a quick creamy dessert that can be served immediately or kept frozen.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.255
posts.body_markdown:
Creamy Banana-Berry Ice blends frozen bananas with lime, frozen berries, and coconut cream into a quick frozen dessert with no cooking.

The bananas are blended first with lime zest and juice until creamy. Frozen berries and coconut cream are added afterward so the final texture can be adjusted as the mixture blends.

It is designed to be served immediately, though the source notes that it can be kept frozen for up to one month. Fresh berries, toasted coconut, or chocolate shavings are optional garnishes.

## Ingredients
- 4 frozen bananas
- Zest and juice of 1 lime
- 2 cups frozen raspberries, blueberries, or strawberries
- 1 cup coconut cream
- Optional garnish: fresh berries, toasted coconut, or chocolate shavings

## Method
Blend the frozen bananas with the lime zest and juice in a blender or food processor until soft and creamy, about 2 minutes. Add the frozen berries and coconut cream and continue blending until the desired consistency is reached. Serve immediately, with any optional garnish if desired. The source notes that the dessert can be kept frozen for up to 1 month. Makes 8–10 servings.

posts.title: Tomato Chutney
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A concentrated tomato chutney with garlic, ginger, cumin, lemon, sugar, chili, and a final spoonful of olive oil.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.258
posts.body_markdown:
Tomato Chutney cooks grated tomatoes down until most of their liquid has evaporated, then sharpens them with garlic, ginger, cumin, lemon, sugar, and chili.

Tomato paste and the seasonings are added only after the fresh tomatoes have reduced. A short final sauté concentrates the mixture without turning it into a long-cooked sauce.

Olive oil goes in at the very end. The source notes that the oil helps preservation, while the small batch size also makes the chutney practical to prepare fresh.

## Ingredients
- 3/4 cup tomatoes, grated
- 3 tablespoons tomato paste
- 1/2 teaspoon garlic, crushed
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, crushed
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 3/4 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 2 teaspoons lemon juice
- 1/2 teaspoon sugar
- 1/2 teaspoon chili powder, or to taste
- 1 tablespoon olive oil

## Method
Sauté the grated tomatoes in a small frying pan over medium heat. When most of the tomato liquid has evaporated, add the tomato paste, garlic, ginger, cumin, salt, lemon juice, sugar, and chili powder. Sauté for 1 minute. Add the olive oil, stir for 30 seconds, then remove from the heat. Serve warm or cool. If desired, store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks; without the oil, the source limits storage to about 2 days. Makes 1/2 cup.

posts.title: Cilantro Mint Chutney
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A fresh cilantro-and-mint chutney blended with lime, oil, and salt, with optional agave and a simple oil-preservation step.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.259
posts.body_markdown:
Cilantro Mint Chutney is a bright green blend of fresh cilantro, mint, lime, salt, oil, and optional agave, processed to a pulpy rather than perfectly smooth texture.

This chutney uses a large proportion of fresh herbs, so the flavor comes primarily from cilantro and mint rather than dried spices. Lime supplies the sharpness and helps loosen the blend.

If the chutney is too chunky, the source suggests adding a little more olive oil or lime juice while blending. A thin layer of oil can also be added for refrigerated storage.

## Ingredients
- 2 bunches fresh cilantro leaves, about 6 cups
- 1 bunch fresh mint leaves, about 3 cups
- 2 teaspoons salt, or to taste
- 3 tablespoons olive or grapeseed oil
- 6 tablespoons lime juice, from about 1–2 limes; lemon may be used
- 1 tablespoon agave nectar, optional
- 1–2 teaspoons olive oil, optional, for preserving

## Method
Combine the cilantro, mint, salt, oil, lime juice, and optional agave in a blender or food processor and blend to a pulp. If the chutney is too chunky, add 1–2 tablespoons more olive oil or lime juice while blending. For storage, place in a sealed container and optionally add 1–2 teaspoons olive oil over the surface. The source gives up to 2 weeks refrigerated storage and up to 1 month frozen. Makes 1 1/2 cups.

posts.title: Cilantro Garlic Chutney
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A pungent green chutney of cilantro, garlic, chili, lime, and olive oil, with an optional coconut variation for a thicker paste.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.260
posts.body_markdown:
Cilantro Garlic Chutney is the more pungent of the source’s two green chutneys, pairing fresh cilantro with garlic, green chili, lime, olive oil, and optional agave.

Garlic and chilies are chopped first in the blender or food processor before the cilantro and remaining ingredients are added. This helps distribute the strongest flavors through the herb base.

The source also gives a coconut variation that thickens the chutney into a more paste-like consistency. Extra lime juice can be used if that version needs more liquid.

## Ingredients
- 4–5 cloves garlic
- 1–3 fresh green chilies
- 2 bunches fresh cilantro leaves, about 1/4 lb (115 g)
- 2 teaspoons salt
- 3 tablespoons olive oil
- 5 tablespoons lime or lemon juice
- 1 tablespoon agave nectar, optional
- Variation: 2–3 tablespoons grated coconut
- For the coconut variation, 1–3 tablespoons extra lime juice if needed

## Method
In a blender or food processor, chop the garlic and green chilies first. Add the cilantro, salt, olive oil, lime or lemon juice, and optional agave and blend to a pulp. For the coconut variation, add 2–3 tablespoons grated coconut and blend to a paste, adding 1–3 tablespoons extra lime juice if needed. The source suggests storing the chutney in a sealed container with 1–2 teaspoons olive oil on top for up to 2 weeks in the refrigerator. Makes 1–1 1/2 cups.

posts.title: Tamarind Chutney
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A sweet-sour tamarind chutney made by soaking the pulp, simmering it with gur, chili, and cumin, then pressing it through a sieve.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.261
posts.body_markdown:
Tamarind Chutney starts by soaking tamarind pulp, then simmering it with gur or brown sugar, chili powder, and cumin for a concentrated sweet-sour condiment.

The soaked pulp is brought to a boil before the remaining ingredients are added. A short five-minute simmer is enough because the main extraction happens during soaking and straining.

Once cooled, the mixture is pushed through a sieve with the back of a spoon. This extracts the tamarind juice while leaving pits, threads, and fibrous pulp behind.

## Ingredients
- 1/2 cup tamarind pulp
- 2 cups water
- 1/2 cup gur or brown sugar
- 2–2 1/2 teaspoons chili powder, or to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon ground cumin

## Method
Rinse the tamarind pulp once under running water, then soak it in the 2 cups water for 30 minutes. Transfer the pulp and soaking water to a medium pot, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a simmer. Add the gur or brown sugar, chili powder, and cumin and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and cool. Press the mixture through a sieve into a bowl, extracting as much tamarind liquid as possible and discarding the pits, threads, and remaining pulp. Store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks. Makes 1 1/2 cups.

posts.title: Coconut Mint Chutney
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A creamy mint chutney of coconut, yogurt, chili, lemon, and optional tomato that rests for 30 minutes so the coconut can thicken it.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.262
posts.body_markdown:
Coconut Mint Chutney blends dry coconut, yogurt, fresh mint, chili, lemon, sweetener, and optional tomato into a smooth, creamy condiment.

Unlike the cilantro chutneys, this mixture is left to stand for at least 30 minutes after blending. That resting time lets the dry coconut absorb liquid and thicken the chutney naturally.

The source keeps the serving quantity small: about a teaspoon is enough alongside snacks, baked pakoras, or curries because the flavor is concentrated.

## Ingredients
- 2 tablespoons unsweetened dry coconut, grated
- 1/2 cup plain yogurt
- 1–3 fresh green chilies
- 1 cup fresh mint leaves
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- Juice of 1 lemon
- 1/2 teaspoon sweetener
- 1/4 cup chopped tomatoes, optional

## Method
Blend the coconut, yogurt, green chilies, mint, salt, lemon juice, sweetener, and optional tomato in a blender or food processor until smooth. Let the chutney stand for at least 30 minutes before serving so the coconut can absorb liquid and the mixture can thicken. Makes about 1 cup.

posts.title: Ripe Mango Chutney
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A quick ripe-mango chutney simmered with cider vinegar, maple syrup, salt, and a little fresh red chili, with nectarine as an alternative.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.262
posts.body_markdown:
Ripe Mango Chutney combines diced ripe mango with apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, salt, and a small amount of fresh red chili.

All of the ingredients go into the pot together and come briefly to a boil before a 15-minute simmer. That short cooking time softens the fruit while keeping the chutney fresh in character.

The source also allows nectarines in place of mangoes. The nectarine version yields slightly less, while the mango version makes about two cups.

## Ingredients
- 3 ripe mangoes, diced, or nectarines
- 1/3 cup apple cider vinegar
- 1/4 cup maple syrup
- Salt to taste
- 1/4 teaspoon fresh red chilies, minced

## Method
Combine the mangoes or nectarines, apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, salt, and red chili in a pot over high heat and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool. Store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week. Makes about 2 cups with mangoes; the source notes about 1 3/4 cups with nectarines.

posts.title: Lime Pickles
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: A two-stage lime pickle: salt-and-turmeric cured slices are simmered in a spiced sweet-sour vinegar syrup, then rested for two weeks.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.263
posts.body_markdown:
Lime Pickles are a long-resting sweet-and-sour condiment in which thin lime slices are first cured with salt and turmeric before being simmered in a spiced vinegar syrup.

The lime slices sit for 2–3 days before the syrup is made. Vinegar, sugar, bay, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, cumin, and cayenne simmer together until thickened.

After a final 10-minute simmer with the limes, the pickles rest for two weeks before use. The syrup needs to keep the slices covered during that curing period.

## Ingredients
- 12 limes or lemons, thinly sliced into circles
- 2–3 teaspoons pickling salt or regular salt
- 1 teaspoon turmeric
- 2 cups apple cider vinegar
- 3 cups sugar; the source uses gur or brown sugar
- 4 bay leaves
- 4 cinnamon sticks
- 6 cloves
- 6 peppercorns
- 1 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- Extra vinegar as needed during curing to keep the lime slices covered

## Method
Spread the lime slices on a baking sheet. Sprinkle one side evenly with half the salt and half the turmeric, turn the slices over, and sprinkle with the remaining salt and turmeric. Leave at room temperature, or in the sun if possible, for 2–3 days. In a pot over low heat, combine the apple cider vinegar, sugar, bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, cumin, and cayenne and simmer for 30 minutes, until the syrup thickens. Add the lime slices and simmer for another 10 minutes. Cool and transfer to a lidded jar, making sure the syrup covers the limes by about 1/4–1/2 inch (1/2–1 cm). Leave at room temperature for 2 weeks, shaking from time to time and topping up with vinegar if the syrup level falls. Refrigerate after curing; the source gives 2–3 months of refrigerated storage. Makes 2 1/2–3 cups.
